transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I'm just really worn down lately. 

For the past year, I've been trying to prove that... well, that someone in the clinic system is changing my dad's lab results. Or holding parts of them back. My family and his doctors just keep telling me the numbers are fine, but... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. It's just... it's exhausting trying to get anyone to see it.

Aside from your concerns about your father's medical records, have you been experiencing any other unusual changes in your life, such as feeling like your thoughts are being broadcasted, hearing voices that others don't, or feeling like you've lost your ability to enjoy things or take care of yourself?

No, nothing like that. I mean... I don't hear things or think people are reading my mind. I'm just trying to figure out what's happening with my dad. 

Other than that... I'm fine. I still go to my shifts at the clinic, I pay my bills, I take care of myself. Everything else is just... normal. I'm just doing my job and living my life.
Have you recently been diagnosed with any new medical conditions or started taking any new medications or supplements?
No. I haven't. I don't take anything. Just... maybe a vitamin sometimes. But no, no new conditions or anything like that. I'm healthy.
How much has this situation with your father's records interfered with your ability to socialize or maintain your relationships with your friends and family?

Um... I guess it's caused some issues. My family... they've started leaving me out of the planning for his appointments lately. They just don't tell me. 

And... at work, I don't know. I just feel like I'm not being considered for lab supervision anymore. People there seem to think I make the record issues... too confrontational. So... yeah. I guess it has affected some things.
Do you feel that your family and coworkers are working together to keep the truth about your father's records from you?
No. I... I don't think they're working together. They don't really know each other. It's just... they all have their own reasons for acting the way they do.
Do you feel that anyone is intentionally trying to harm you or discredit you because of your discovery regarding your father's records?
No. Um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really... nobody is trying to hurt me. It's just what I already told you. I don't think it's anything like that.
When you have tried to show your family or the doctors the specific discrepancies you see in the records, how do they explain the differences to you?

Um... they don't really explain it. They just tell me the numbers are fine. 

But... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I've been trying to prove it for the past year... that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his lab results. And... no matter how many doctors or family members I show, they just keep saying it's fine. It's... it's really wearing me down.
Aside from your concerns about your father's medical records, do you have any other beliefs or ideas that other people might find difficult to believe or disagree with?
No. Um... no, I don't. I don't really know what you mean by that. It's... it's just the records. Everything else in my life is just normal.
Are there any specific pieces of evidence or documents that you have personally collected or saved that you believe prove the records have been altered?
No. Um... I don't have a file or anything like that. I didn't take any documents. I just... I know what I saw. That's all.

If I were able to show you definitive, verifiable proof from multiple independent sources that the lab records you saw were accurate and unchanged, would you be willing to accept that your original conclusion might be incorrect?

I... no. I don't think I would. 

Because... like I already said, I know what I saw. I've spent a whole year trying to prove that someone in the system is changing or holding back my dad's results. So... if you brought me proof, I'd just think... I don't know, that it was part of it. 

It doesn't matter how many doctors or people tell me the numbers are fine. I know they aren't. It's just... it's really wearing me down having to keep explaining this.
